chapters.1: God tells Jonah to go preach to Nineveh, but Jonah instead boards a ship fleeing in the opposite direction. God sends a violent storm, the sailors realize Jonah is the cause and throw him overboard at his own suggestion, and a great fish swallows him.
chapters.2: From inside the fish, Jonah prays to God, describing his near-drowning and crediting God for saving his life even in the depths of the sea. He ends the prayer with a vow of thanksgiving, and God causes the fish to vomit him out onto dry land.
chapters.3: God repeats his command and this time Jonah goes to Nineveh, warning that the city will be destroyed in forty days. The king and all the people respond with genuine repentance, fasting and turning from violence, and God relents and spares the city.
chapters.4: Jonah is angry rather than glad that Nineveh was spared, admitting he fled earlier because he knew God would be merciful to them. God uses a plant that gives Jonah shade and then withers to make a point: if Jonah can care about a plant, God can rightly care about sparing a great city full of people.
